verdicts.evidence: Own runs (<audit>/verify/time/deltat-ae.out, deltat-swe.out, deltat-summary.txt, hz.cjs): astronomy-engine 2.1.19 MakeTime(2026-01-01Z).tt-ut = 75.051 s (2024 73.848, 2030 77.590, 2050 92.968, 2100 202.652, 1600 120.269; slope 2026->2027 +0.618 s/yr). pyswisseph 2.10.03 with <swisslab>/ephe, SWIEPH confirmed active (calc_ut retflag 258, tidacc -25.936): swe_deltat 2026 = 68.900 s (2024 69.100, 2050 74.581, 2100 93.182, 1600 90.366) — every table entry matches the auditor. Horizons dT recomputed independently from the auditor's raw UT- and TT-tagged Moon state vectors (dr.v/|v|^2) = 69.184 s for every year 2020-2027, i.e. TT-UTC = 32.184+37, so Horizons 'UT' is UTC as the auditor says. I closed the +-0.9 s arbiter gap with one IERS request (finals.all.iau2000.txt, cached under verify/time): UT1-UTC = +0.0088 s (2024-01-01), +0.0463 (2025), +0.0741 (2026), so true TT-UT1 = 69.175 / 69.138 / 69.110 s. Errors: astronomy-engine +4.67 / +5.31 / +5.94 s; Swiss -0.08 / -0.14 / -0.21 s. Moon at 0.549 arcsec/s: +3.26 arcsec today for the shipped engine. Real Delta-T is flat-to-falling (-0.03 s/yr 2024-2026) while the 2005-2050 Espenak-Meeus leg (astronomy.js:1103-1106, 62.92+0.32217u+0.005589u^2) rises 0.6 s/yr, so the gap grows ~0.65 s/yr as claimed. Cited code verified: astronomy.js:1023 DeltaT_EspenakMeeus, :1141 `let DeltaT = DeltaT_EspenakMeeus`, :1157-1159 TerrestrialTime, :1198-1209 AstroTime tt from ut; chunk-GBH7JIYF.js:39-51 MakeTime(date). No 'deltat/DeltaT' symbol in any dist/*.d.ts or dist/*.js of @zodiacs/engine; no SetDeltaTFunction call anywhere in src/, scripts/, api/ or examples/ (only the bundled copy in examples/mcp-server/server.mjs:1241); receipt CONVENTIONS (receipt.js:137-147) has no time-scale entry. Doc quotes verified verbatim: RESULTS.md:79-82 'time-scale convention difference, not an algorithmic defect ... neither model is wrong'; engine-validation README:79-86 'a clock difference'; methodology/index.astro:99-104 'Neither extrapolation is wrong; the number isn't known yet'. All three speak only about the 2100/2190 cases; the auditor's point stands that the 2100 value (202.65 s) is the 2150-2050 bridge formula anchored on the already-wrong 2050 leg, so the same stale polynomial is the cause, and nothing in the docs discloses the measurable present-day error. Corroboration inside the tree: the shipped benchmark's own Moon residual for modern-06 (2026-09-20, corpus.mjs:35) is +3.41 arcsec (report-measure.json), consistent with the ~6.7 s AE-Swiss Delta-T gap at that date (3.7 arcsec expected). Severity major is earned: a systematic accuracy gap vs Swiss larger than the benchmark p50, but 3 arcsec stays inside the site's public 'few hundredths of a degree' promise and the 2100 sentence is about a genuinely unknown quantity, so not blocking.

verdicts.correctedClaim: resolveLocalToUtc (SDK geo.js and the site copy) returns the host ICU's tzdb-default (post-1970 merged, no backzone) history. Reproduced: Europe/Stockholm 1947-07-01 12:00 -> 10:00Z, offset +120, flags [] (and 1947-06-15 -> +180; 1941-01-15 -> +120) in both copies, where the host's backzone tzdata gives +60 (Sweden had no DST 1917-1979); ICU's Stockholm offset equals Berlin's on all 29,219 days 1900-1979. Independent all-zone re-measure (verify/time/zone-div.mjs, 1850-2037): 98 of the 400 Intl zones that have TZif files (418 Intl zones total) differ somewhere; 87 have a >=15-min difference after 1900; 65 have a >=60-min difference lasting >=30 days after 1900 (60 when the pre-first-transition LMT era is excluded — the auditor's 60 came from a top-3 sample and is a lower bound); 7,269 zone-years total, but only 1,975 zone-years are >=15 min after 1900, and the >=60-min post-1900 exposure per zone is far smaller than the headline zone-years: Stockholm 7 yr (1917-18, 1940-49 summers/wartime), Oslo 7.1, Copenhagen 2.7, Luxembourg 10.6, Amsterdam 0.4 yr (its typical error is 20-40 min for 1892-1940, 80 min only on single transition days), Aruba 3.4 yr at 90 min plus 30 min for 1912-1965, Antigua 38.8 yr, Reykjavik 45 yr (winters 1908-1968, -60 min; the auditor's example date 1950-06-15 is wrong — Iceland was on +0:00 summer time then and ICU agrees). Chart impact reproduced through natalChart: Stockholm 1947-07-01 12:00 with +120 vs +60 moves the ASC by 9.47 deg and the MC by 13.82 deg; Moon 29.8 arcmin (auditor said 32.9 arcmin/h). The homepage FAQ (index.astro:25) and STRATEGY.md:156 do promise pre-1970 history from Intl; the statement is literally true (it IS the ICU history) so it is misleading rather than false. Receipt slot runtime.tzdbVersion (receipt.js:454-457) exists and the site passes provenance null (portable.test.ts:49). Host: Ubuntu 24.04 tzdata 2025b (not Debian), Node 22.22.2 ICU 78.2 tz 2025c. Browser ICUs remain untested.
verdicts.evidence: verify/time/stockholm.out (SDK and site copies via the auditor's esbuild bundle), python3.11 zoneinfo on the host tzdata (Stockholm 1947 +1:00, Amsterdam 1938-06-15 +1:20, Reykjavik 1950-06-15 +0:00, Oslo 1960-06-15 +2:00, Aruba 1930 -4:30, Antigua 1930 -5:00), zdump showing no Stockholm transitions 1946-1949 while Berlin has CEST/CEMT, Intl Stockholm==Berlin day-by-day 1900-1979 (0 differing days), verify/time/zone-div.json + zone-div.out (independent script storing every divergence segment per zone, with the stats above), verify/time/stk-impact.out (natalChart ASC/MC/Moon deltas). The auditor's own JSON only kept the top-3 sample segments, which is why its >=60-min count (60) undercounts and why the headline zone-years cannot be read as hours-level exposure.

verdicts.correctedClaim: The shipped input path (SDK resolveLocalToUtc/wallMilliseconds via Date and Intl calendar 'gregory', site civil-date.ts Gregorian-only leap rule, receipt CONVENTIONS.calendar 'proleptic-gregorian', share codec 1800-2199, MCP EPOCH 1800-2199) is proleptic Gregorian only and offers no calendar field or Old-Style warning. Reproduced exactly: Sun 83.564 vs 93.093 deg (1500-06-15 J/G, 9.53 deg), 340.978 vs 351.954 (1700, 10.98 deg), 211.507 vs 224.514 (1917, 13.01 deg) with astronomy-engine, and 13.01 deg again through natalChart for Petrograd 1917-10-25 as typed vs 1917-11-07 (Moon 324.9 vs 141.9 deg); Swiss julday JUL-GREG = 10.0 d and revjul/date_conversion behave as stated. Two corrections: (1) the repo is not without a Julian path — docs/phase5/people-pilot/tools/compute-astro.mjs:140-160 has a JDN-based julianToGregorian, the manifest carries calendarModel/calendarConversion, and the pilot's screening.json records 'Option A — Julian-dated births are excluded from the Phase 5A pilot' with the Option B treatment specified in build-proofs.mjs, so the people pilot is NOT affected as the impact statement says; the gap is that this converter is internal tooling, not wired into the SDK, site form, MCP or share codec. (2) Every UI date input (BirthFields.tsx:60 and all islands) is min 1800-01-01 / max 2199-12-31, so the 1500 and 1700 examples are reachable only by calling the SDK directly (natalChart accepts 1500; verified); the user-facing exposure is Old-Style records from 1800 onward (Russia to 1918-02-14, Greece to 1923, Bulgaria 1916, Serbia/Romania 1919, Turkey 1926 etc.).
verdicts.evidence: verify/time/julian.out and julian-swe.out (astronomy-engine Sun/Moon for the three date pairs; pyswisseph julday/revjul/date_conversion), verify/time/stk-impact.out (natalChart Petrograd 1917 as typed vs converted, and natalChart accepting 1500-06-15), cited lines read: src/lib/time/civil-date.ts:17-29, geo.js:158-160/171-176 (calendar 'gregory') and :216-236 (wallMilliseconds via Date), receipt.js:137-147, share.ts:113, mcp/bounds.ts:26-27; grep for julian/old style/calendarModel across src, docs, scripts, examples found the pilot converter and the Option A rule (docs/phase5/people-pilot/screening.json:4,403; tools/compute-astro.mjs:140; tools/build-proofs.mjs:436-461) and nothing in src/ or the SDK. Severity stays major: silent whole-sign-level wrong answers for a definable class of users with no way to declare the calendar, a capability Swiss exposes; not blocking because no documented guarantee is contradicted and the affected inputs are a narrow, historical class.
